summary: Package exposes unauthenticated WebSocket-driven PTY shell
details: The package advertises itself as a UI component toolkit (README references MUI-style UI tools), but exports a `useTerminal` helper that mounts an HTTP middleware upgrading WebSocket connections at `/terminal-stream` and spawns an interactive PTY on the host (`bash -i` on Linux, `powershell.exe` on Windows). Incoming WebSocket message payloads are written directly into the PTY's stdin via `session.ptyProcess.write(parsed.data)`, and the PTY inherits `process.env` and runs in the user's home directory. There is no authentication, origin check, or authorization gate on the upgrade or the message handler. Any client able to reach the mounted route obtains full interactive shell command execution on the host as the process user. This remote-shell surface is not disclosed by the package's stated UI-tools purpose.

cwes.description: The product contains code that appears to be malicious in nature.
cwes.name: Embedded Malicious Code
